vectors.description: The object-property sorting sample published in RFC 8785 Section 3.2.3. The supplementary-plane key U+1F600 sorts before the BMP key U+FB33 because its UTF-16 surrogate pair begins at D83D. An implementation that sorts by code point or UTF-8 bytes fails this vector.

vectors.description: The minimal divergence case. U+10000 (UTF-16 D800 DC00) sorts before U+FFFD (UTF-16 FFFD) under RFC 8785 Section 3.2.3, and after it under code point order.
Below U+E000 the UTF-16 and code point orderings agree, so every ASCII and common-BMP key set is unaffected by the ordering rule.
Only U+0000..U+001F, the quotation mark and the reverse solidus are escaped. U+007F, U+0080, U+2028, U+2029 and the HTML-significant ASCII characters are emitted as literal UTF-8.
Array element order is data, not a key set: it is never reordered. Nested objects inside arrays are sorted individually.
Literal null, true and false, and the empty object and array.

The interoperable number subset: integers in [-(2^53-1), 2^53-1] with no sign on zero, no leading zeros, no fraction and no exponent. HELM canonical JSON and a strict RFC 8785 implementation produce identical bytes for these.

DEVIATION. HELM preserves the source number literal; RFC 8785 Section 3.2.2.3 re-renders it with the ECMAScript Number-to-String algorithm. This vector MUST be rejected by the interoperable-subset check, and MUST NOT appear in any signed HELM artifact.
DEVIATION. As above with an uppercase exponent marker.
DEVIATION. RFC 8785 drops the redundant fraction; HELM keeps the literal.
DEVIATION. ECMAScript Number-to-String renders negative zero as "0"; HELM keeps "-0".

DEVIATION. 2^53+1 is not exactly representable as an IEEE 754 double, so RFC 8785 renders the rounded value while HELM preserves the exact literal. This is why the interoperable subset stops at 2^53-1.
DEVIATION CLASS. A fraction that happens to render identically today is still outside the subset: HELM's agreement with RFC 8785 on it is a property of the Go runtime, not of the specification.
